source: That mortal man should feed upon the creature that feeds his lamp, and, like Stubb, eat him by his own light, as you may say; this seems so outlandish a thing that one must needs go a little into the history and philosophy of it.

It is upon record, that three centuries ago the tongue of the Right Whale was esteemed a great delicacy in France, and commanded large prices there. Also, that in Henry VIIIth’s time, a certain cook of the court obtained a handsome reward for inventing an admirable sauce to be eaten with barbacued porpoises, which, you remember, are a species of whale. Porpoises, indeed, are to this day considered fine eating. The meat is made into balls about the size of billiard balls, and being well seasoned and spiced might be taken for turtle-balls or veal balls. The old monks of Dunfermline were very fond of them. They had a great porpoise grant from the crown.

The fact is, that among his hunters at least, the whale would by all hands be considered a noble dish, were there not so much of him; but when you come to sit down before a meat-pie nearly one hundred feet long, it takes away your appetite. Only the most unprejudiced of men like Stubb, nowadays partake of cooked whales; but the Esquimaux are not so fastidious. We all know how they live upon whales, and have rare old vintages of prime old train oil. Zogranda, one of their most famous doctors, recommends strips of blubber for infants, as being exceedingly juicy and nourishing. And this reminds me that certain Englishmen, who long ago were accidentally left in Greenland by a whaling vessel—that these men actually lived for several months on the mouldy scraps of whales which had been left ashore after trying out the blubber. Among the Dutch whalemen these scraps are called “fritters”; which, indeed, they greatly resemble, being brown and crisp, and smelling something like old Amsterdam housewives’ dough-nuts or oly-cooks, when fresh. They have such an eatable look that the most self-denying stranger can hardly keep his hands off.

But what further depreciates the whale as a civilized dish, is his exceeding richness. He is the great prize ox of the sea, too fat to be delicately good. Look at his hump, which would be as fine eating as the buffalo’s (which is esteemed a rare dish), were it not such a solid pyramid of fat. But the spermaceti itself, how bland and creamy that is; like the transparent, half-jellied, white meat of a cocoanut in the third month of its growth, yet far too rich to supply a substitute for butter. Nevertheless, many whalemen have a method of absorbing it into some other substance, and then partaking of it. In the long try watches of the night it is a common thing for the seamen to dip their ship-biscuit into the huge oil-pots and let them fry there awhile. Many a good supper have I thus made.

In the case of a small Sperm Whale the brains are accounted a fine dish. The casket of the skull is broken into with an axe, and the two plump, whitish lobes being withdrawn (precisely resembling two large puddings), they are then mixed with flour, and cooked into a most delectable mess, in flavor somewhat resembling calves’ head, which is quite a dish among some epicures; and every one knows that some young bucks among the epicures, by continually dining upon calves’ brains, by and by get to have a little brains of their own, so as to be able to tell a calf’s head from their own heads; which, indeed, requires uncommon discrimination. And that is the reason why a young buck with an intelligent looking calf’s head before him, is somehow one of the saddest sights you can see. The head looks a sort of reproachfully at him, with an “Et tu Brute!” expression.

It is not, perhaps, entirely because the whale is so excessively unctuous that landsmen seem to regard the eating of him with abhorrence; that appears to result, in some way, from the consideration before mentioned: i.e. that a man should eat a newly murdered thing of the sea, and eat it too by its own light. But no doubt the first man that ever murdered an ox was regarded as a murderer; perhaps he was hung; and if he had been put on his trial by oxen, he certainly would have been; and he certainly deserved it if any murderer does. Go to the meat-market of a Saturday night and see the crowds of live bipeds staring up at the long rows of dead quadrupeds. Does not that sight take a tooth out of the cannibal’s jaw? Cannibals? who is not a cannibal? I tell you it will be more tolerable for the Fejee that salted down a lean missionary in his cellar against a coming famine; it will be more tolerable for that provident Fejee, I say, in the day of judgment, than for thee, civilized and enlightened gourmand, who nailest geese to the ground and feastest on their bloated livers in thy paté-de-foie-gras.

But Stubb, he eats the whale by its own light, does he? and that is adding insult to injury, is it? Look at your knife-handle, there, my civilized and enlightened gourmand dining off that roast beef, what is that handle made of?—what but the bones of the brother of the very ox you are eating? And what do you pick your teeth with, after devouring that fat goose? With a feather of the same fowl. And with what quill did the Secretary of the Society for the Suppression of Cruelty to Ganders formally indite his circulars? It is only within the last month or two that that society passed a resolution to patronize nothing but steel pens.

modern_da.title: Kapitel 65 — Hvalen som ret
paragraphs: At et dødeligt menneske skal spise netop det dyr, der giver olie til hans lampe, og, som Stubb, så at sige spise det ved dets eget lys, forekommer så besynderligt, at vi må se lidt nærmere på dets historie og filosofi.

Optegnelserne viser, at retvalens tunge for tre hundrede år siden blev anset for en stor delikatesse i Frankrig, hvor den kunne indbringe høje priser. De viser også, at en bestemt hofkok på Henrik den Ottendes tid vandt en flot belønning for at opfinde en udmærket sovs til grillede marsvin, som, du vil huske, er en slags hval. Marsvin regnes i øvrigt stadig for fin mad i dag. Kødet rulles til kugler på størrelse med billardkugler, og når det er godt krydret, kunne det gå for skildpaddekugler eller kalvekugler. De gamle munke i Dunfermline holdt af dem. Kronen havde givet dem en stor tildeling af marsvin.

Sagen er, at hvalen, i hvert fald blandt dem, der jager den, ville blive anset af alle mand for en fornem ret, hvis der ikke var så meget af den. Men når man sætter sig foran en kødpie på næsten hundrede fod i længden, tager det appetitten fra en. Kun de mest fordomsfri mænd, som Stubb, spiser kogt hval nu om dage. Men eskimoerne er ikke så kræsne. Vi ved alle, hvordan de lever af hvaler og gemmer sjældne gamle årgange af fineste tran. Zogranda, en af deres mest berømte læger, anbefaler strimler af spæk til spædbørn, fordi det er usædvanlig saftigt og nærende. Og det minder mig om nogle englændere, som for længe siden ved et uheld blev efterladt i Grønland af et hvalfangerskib. Disse mænd levede faktisk i flere måneder af de beskimlede rester af hvaler, som var blevet liggende på land, efter at spækket var blevet kogt ud (kogt ned til olie). Blandt de hollandske hvalfangere kaldes disse rester »fritter«, og det ligner de såmænd meget, for de er brune og sprøde, og når de er friske, lugter de lidt som gamle amsterdamske husmødres æbleskiver, eller oly-cooks. De ser så spiselige ud, at den mest selvovervindende fremmede næsten ikke kan holde fingrene fra dem.

Men det, der yderligere trækker hvalen ned som civiliseret ret, er dens overvældende fedme. Den er havets store præmieokse, for fed til at være delikat god. Se på dens pukkel, som ville være lige så fin at spise som bøfflens (som regnes for en sjælden ret), hvis den ikke var sådan en massiv pyramide af fedt. Men selve spermacetien, hvor mild og cremet den er, som det gennemsigtige, halvt geléagtige hvide kød i en kokosnød i dens tredje vækstmåned. Alligevel er den langt for fed til at kunne træde i stedet for smør. Ikke desto mindre har mange hvalfangere en måde at få den opsuget i et andet stof og spise den på. I de lange kogevagter om natten er det almindeligt, at sømændene dypper deres skibskiks i de store oliegryder og lader dem stege der et stykke tid. Jeg har fået mangen en god aftensmad på den måde.

Ved en lille kaskelot regnes hjernen for en fin ret. Hovedskallens kiste brydes op med en økse, og de to buttede, hvidlige lapper trækkes ud (de ligner nøjagtigt to store buddinger). Så blandes de med mel og stoppes til en overordentlig lækker ret, der i smag minder lidt om kalvehoved, som er en stor ret blandt visse fine smagsdommere. Og alle ved, at nogle unge laps blandt disse fine smagsdommere ved stadig at spise kalvehjerner efterhånden får en smule hjerne selv, nok til at kunne kende forskel på et kalvehoved og deres eget hoved — hvilket i sandhed kræver en usædvanlig skelneevne. Og derfor er en ung laps med et intelligent udseende kalvehoved foran sig på en eller anden måde et af de tristeste syn, man kan se. Hovedet ser på ham på en bebrejdende måde med et »Et tu, Brute!«-udtryk.

Måske er det ikke helt og holdent, fordi hvalen er så overordentlig olieagtig, at landkrabber synes, tanken om at spise den er afskyelig. Det kommer på en eller anden måde af det, der allerede er sagt: at et menneske skal spise en nylig myrdet skabning fra havet, og endda spise den ved dens eget lys. Men uden tvivl blev den første mand, der nogensinde myrdede en okse, regnet for en morder. Måske hængte de ham, og hvis okserne havde stillet ham for retten, havde de helt sikkert gjort det. Og han fortjente det, om nogen morder gør. Gå hen på kødmarkedet en lørdag aften og se på mængderne af levende tobenede, der stirrer op på de lange rækker af døde firbenede. Slår det ikke en tand ud af kannibalens kæbe? Kannibaler? Hvem er ikke kannibal? Jeg siger jer, det bliver mere udholdeligt på dommens dag for fijianeren, der saltede en mager missionær ned i sin kælder for at klare sig gennem en kommende hungersnød — mere udholdeligt for den forudseende fijianer, siger jeg — end for jer, civiliserede og oplyste fråsere, der nagler gæs fast til gulvet og fester på deres opsvulmede lever i jeres pâté de foie gras.

Men Stubb spiser hvalen ved dens eget lys, gør han? Og det er at lægge fornærmelse til skade, er det? Kig på dit knivskaft derhenne, min civiliserede og oplyste fråser, mens du spiser den steg. Hvad er skaftet lavet af? Hvad andet end knoglerne fra broren til netop den okse, du spiser? Og hvad piller du tænder med, når du er færdig med den fede gås? En fjer fra samme fugl. Og hvilken pen brugte sekretæren for Selskabet til Bekæmpelse af Grusomhed mod Gasser til at skrive sine officielle rundskrivelser? Først for en måned eller to siden har det selskab vedtaget kun at bruge stålpenne.
